README.md:526:### Checkpoint Remote
README.md:528:By default, checkpoint data rides along with your own pushes — but only to **one** remote, the elected checkpoint sync remote. Entire picks it in this order:
README.md:530:1. `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote`, if set. This is fail-closed: if it names a remote that isn't configured, checkpoints don't sync.
README.md:531:2. A remote captured from your own habits: the first push whose target matches the branch's declared push destination elects that remote, announces it on stderr, and carries the checkpoints. The first capture sticks.
README.md:536:A push to any *other* remote carries no checkpoint data. `entire status` shows the current destination, where it came from, and how many checkpoints are unpushed. This matters if you push code to several remotes: checkpoints go to exactly one of them.
README.md:538:If instead you want checkpoint data in a separate repo (e.g., a private repo for a public project), configure `checkpoint_remote` with a structured provider and repo. A dedicated `checkpoint_remote` is addressed directly and is exempt from the single-remote election above:
README.md:543:    "checkpoint_remote": {
README.md:545:      "repo": "myorg/checkpoints-private"
README.md:554:entire enable --checkpoint-remote github:myorg/checkpoints-private
README.md:557:Entire derives the git URL automatically using the same protocol (SSH or HTTPS) as your push remote. It will:
README.md:559:- Fetch existing checkpoint data locally if the remote has it and you don't (one-time)
README.md:560:- Push checkpoint data to the checkpoint repo instead of your default push remote
README.md:561:- Ignore the setting if it looks inherited rather than yours, and fall back to `origin` (or, failing that, the remote you are pushing to). `checkpoint_remote` is normally committed in `.entire/settings.json`, so cloning or forking a project inherits it — without this, a contributor's session data would be pushed into the upstream project's checkpoint repo. A setting is treated as yours when it lives in the gitignored `.entire/settings.local.json`, or when your `origin` **and every push URL** of the remote you are pushing to are owned by the same account or org as the checkpoint repo. Requiring the push destination too covers contributors who cloned the upstream repo and added their own fork, where `origin` belongs to the upstream project rather than to them; requiring every push URL covers mirror-style remotes that fan out to several repositories
README.md:562:- If your checkpoint repo is owned by a different account or org than `origin`, configure it in `.entire/settings.local.json` so it is always honored
README.md:567:`ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` allows you to provide a dedicated token for checkpoint repository operations, without modifying the credentials used for your primary repository.
README.md:569:When this environment variable is set, Entire behaves as follows:
README.md:571:- Injects the token into HTTPS Git operations used for checkpoint fetch and push
README.md:572:- If `checkpoint_remote` is configured:
README.md:573:  - Prefers an HTTPS URL for the checkpoint remote when a token is present, even if the repository’s `origin` uses SSH
README.md:574:- If `checkpoint_remote` is not configured:
README.md:576:- If `checkpoint_remote` configuration cannot be loaded:
README.md:578:  - If `origin` is a valid SSH or HTTPS Git remote, Entire converts it to an HTTPS URL to enable token-based authentication
README.md:582:When enabled, Entire automatically generates AI summaries for checkpoints at commit time. Summaries capture intent, outcome, learnings, friction points, and open items from the session.

README.md:629:Entire automatically redacts detected secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) from transcripts and metadata before writing a checkpoint, but redaction is best-effort.
README.md:631:The temporary shadow branches used during a session get the same redaction for transcripts and metadata, but their **code-file snapshots are raw blobs of your working tree**, so a secret hardcoded in your source appears unredacted there. Entire never pushes shadow branches — don't push them manually. See [docs/security-and-privacy.md](docs/security-and-privacy.md) for the full picture, including the configurable scanner layers, opt-in PII redaction, and the OpenAI Privacy Filter pass.

agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:5:Kilo Code is a fork of OpenCode with a `@kilocode/plugin` API that exposes session lifecycle events on its internal event bus. Plugins are TypeScript/JavaScript modules loaded at startup from `.kilo/plugins/` and run on Bun. The integration installs a project plugin that subscribes to the bus and forwards five lifecycle hooks (`session-start`, `turn-start`, `turn-end`, `compaction`, `session-end`) to the Entire CLI. The plugin uses Kilo's native event bus directly — `session.idle` is deprecated upstream and `session.status` with `status.type === "idle"` is the reliable turn-end signal in both interactive and `kilo run` modes.

agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:104:- **Resume restore is EXPERIMENTAL / incomplete.** Kilo keeps sessions in a global store (`~/.local/share/kilo/kilo.db`) keyed by session id, not in `.entire/`. `entire resume` restores the transcript to `.entire/tmp/kilo/<id>.json` and prints `kilo run --session <id>`, but Kilo only reads its own store — so resume works **only while Kilo still has the session locally**. Restoring a session Entire has but Kilo does not (after `kilo session delete`, a fresh clone, or another machine) is **not yet supported**: it would require importing the session back into Kilo via `kilo import <file>` (Kilo exposes `kilo export [id]` / `kilo import <file>` for this). That needs the durable artifact to be Kilo's native export blob rather than the analysis-oriented JSONL stored today, and is tracked as future work. Everything else (checkpointing, attribution, summaries, transcript analysis) is unaffected. The agent is `is_preview: true` accordingly.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:105:- Kilo plugins do not load when `KILO_PURE=1` is set. The plugin must not assume that env is unset; if it is set, hooks never fire and `are-hooks-installed` still returns true (file exists).
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:106:- The transcript is materialized by `prepare-transcript` (Go side, via `kilo session show --format json` — see `command_runner.go`), which Entire calls before reading, mirroring the OpenCode parent. The plugin's `turn-end` fires **synchronously** and carries only `session_id` + `model`: `kilo run` exits on the same idle event, so an awaited in-plugin fetch could be cancelled before the hook runs. Turn-end payloads that do carry messages are still honored, but an empty message set never overwrites an existing transcript.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:107:- `session.idle` is deprecated upstream and not reliably emitted in `kilo run` mode. The plugin subscribes to `session.status` and filters on `status.type === "idle"` for turn-end.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:108:- Sub-sessions (Kilo subagent threads) are filtered out at `session.created` time by checking `info.parentID`. Subagent activity inside the parent session is still captured because the parent session JSON includes all parts.

build/README.md:1:# External Agents for Entire CLI
build/README.md:3:This repository contains standalone external agent binaries that extend the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) with support for additional AI coding agents.
build/README.md:7:External agents are standalone binaries (named `entire-agent-<name>`) that teach Entire CLI how to work with AI coding agents it doesn't natively support. When an external agent is installed on your `PATH`, Entire discovers it automatically and gains the ability to:
build/README.md:9:- **Create checkpoints** during AI coding sessions so you can rewind mistakes
build/README.md:10:- **Capture transcripts** of what the AI agent did and why
build/README.md:11:- **Install hooks** so the AI agent's lifecycle events (start, stop, commit) flow through Entire
build/README.md:13:External agents communicate with Entire CLI via subcommands that accept and return JSON over stdin/stdout. See the [external agent protocol spec](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md) for the full interface.
build/README.md:19:| [Kiro](agents/entire-agent-kiro/) | `agents/entire-agent-kiro/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis |
build/README.md:20:| [Amp](agents/entire-agent-amp/) | `agents/entire-agent-amp/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + token calculation + compact transcripts |
build/README.md:21:| [Qwen Code](agents/entire-agent-qwen/) | `agents/entire-agent-qwen/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + compact transcripts |
build/README.md:22:| [Grok Build](agents/entire-agent-grok/) | `agents/entire-agent-grok/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + compact transcripts |
build/README.md:23:| [Oh My Pi](agents/entire-agent-omp/) | `agents/entire-agent-omp/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + compact transcripts |
build/README.md:24:| [Kilo](agents/entire-agent-kilo/) | `agents/entire-agent-kilo/` | Implemented (preview) — hooks + transcript analysis + token calculation + compact transcripts |
build/README.md:30:External agent discovery is opt-in. Once an `entire-agent-<name>` binary is on your `PATH`, set `external_agents: true` in the repo's `.entire/settings.json` so Entire scans for it:
build/README.md:38:Without this flag, Entire ignores external agent binaries even when they're installed.

The stable Entire sidecar transcript lives in a repo-scoped OS temp directory, with a small `.entire/tmp/<session>.json` marker for Entire session discovery. Qwen Code must execute actual tools for checkpoints; local model backends that only print XML-style tool tags as text will not fire Qwen `PostToolUse` hooks.

build/README.md:70:The adapter installs Grok command hooks in `.grok/hooks/entire.json` and reads native transcripts from `~/.grok/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>/chat_history.jsonl`. Project hooks require folder trust (`/hooks-trust` or `--trust`) before they execute, and until the folder is trusted Grok skips them silently, so nothing is captured.
build/README.md:72:Restored sessions can be resumed with `grok --resume <session-id>`, but not at full fidelity: Grok's `encrypted_content` reasoning state is stripped before storage, so a resumed session replays the conversation without its prior reasoning context. Sessions captured before this behaviour shipped cannot be resumed at all. See the [agent README](agents/entire-agent-grok/README.md#session-restore-and-resume).

agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:42:- Session ID source: `parse-hook` resolves identity in this order: (1) explicit IDE session ID (`session_id` / `sessionId` / `chatSessionId`) in the hook payload — populates both `entire_session_id` and `ide_session_id`; (2) explicit CLI `conversation_id` in the payload — populates `entire_session_id` and `conversation_id` only, leaving `ide_session_id` empty so transcript capture skips the IDE path (otherwise a repo with leftover IDE workspace data would silently checkpoint an unrelated IDE chat for what is actually a CLI turn); (3) the most-recently-modified `<sessionId>.json` file in the IDE workspace-sessions directory — Kiro writes the user's prompt or assistant's response to the active chat's transcript file before invoking the hook, so file mtime is the closest signal to "which chat tab fired"; the IDE session UUID is used as both `ide_session_id` and `entire_session_id`; (4) repo-global `kiro-active-session` cache (Kiro CLI / non-IDE flow); (5) CLI `conversation_id` queried from the SQLite DB; (6) a generated Entire ID
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:43:- Session cache: `.entire/tmp/kiro-active-session` is used exclusively for the Kiro-CLI (non-IDE) flow. IDE chats aren't cached as a "current session" because re-deriving from `<sessionId>.json` mtime each turn is what lets tab-switching scenarios resolve correctly
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:44:- Active turn cache: `.entire/tmp/kiro-active-turn` holds the IDE session ID for the in-flight turn — written at `user-prompt-submit`, read by `post-tool-use` and `stop`, cleared at end of `stop`. This binds an entire turn (prompt → tool uses → stop) to the chat that fired prompt-submit, so a tab switch mid-turn cannot cause stop to finalize against a different chat
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:45:- Per-chat trim offset: every IDE chat and every CLI `conversation_id` gets its own offset file (`.entire/tmp/kiro-transcript-offset-<key>.json`) so capturing one chat never trims another chat's history
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:46:- Per-chat tool-call capture: `post-tool-use` appends to a per-chat file (`.entire/tmp/kiro-tool-calls-<sanitized-id>.jsonl`) keyed by the active-turn cache; transcript capture reads only the current chat's file. The legacy global file is reserved for CLI-only flows where there is no IDE chat ID
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:49:- `kiro-active-turn` is a single repo-global file. Each prompt-submit overwrites it; each stop owner-checks before clearing. This is correct for the common cases — single chat, tab-switch mid-turn, sequential turns across tabs, and concurrent CLI+IDE activity (each side's payload lets the other flow stay isolated). It is best-effort under truly overlapping IDE turns (`A prompt → B prompt → A stop`): A's stop has no payload signal that distinguishes it from B's, so the resolver returns whichever IDE chat is currently in cache. The owner-check at clear time prevents A's stop from deleting B's binding, but A's session_id will still resolve to whatever the cache currently holds. Fixing this fully requires a per-turn signal in the hook payload from Kiro, which it does not provide today
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:50:- For the same reason, post-tool-use hooks during a truly overlapping IDE turn fall back to mtime-based active-chat detection when the cache holds the wrong chat. CLI flows are unaffected because they short-circuit on payload `conversation_id`

build/agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:5:Kilo Code is a fork of OpenCode with a `@kilocode/plugin` API that exposes session lifecycle events on its internal event bus. Plugins are TypeScript/JavaScript modules loaded at startup from `.kilo/plugins/` and run on Bun. The integration installs a project plugin that subscribes to the bus and forwards five lifecycle hooks (`session-start`, `turn-start`, `turn-end`, `compaction`, `session-end`) to the Entire CLI. The plugin uses Kilo's native event bus directly — `session.idle` is deprecated upstream and `session.status` with `status.type === "idle"` is the reliable turn-end signal in both interactive and `kilo run` modes.

Project plugins require launching Amp with `PLUGINS=all` in classic Amp clients. build/agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:49:- `kiro-active-turn` is a single repo-global file. Each prompt-submit overwrites it; each stop owner-checks before clearing. This is correct for the common cases — single chat, tab-switch mid-turn, sequential turns across tabs, and concurrent CLI+IDE activity (each side's payload lets the other flow stay isolated). It is best-effort under truly overlapping IDE turns (`A prompt → B prompt → A stop`): A's stop has no payload signal that distinguishes it from B's, so the resolver returns whichever IDE chat is currently in cache. The owner-check at clear time prevents A's stop from deleting B's binding, but A's session_id will still resolve to whatever the cache currently holds. Fixing this fully requires a per-turn signal in the hook payload from Kiro, which it does not provide today

agents/entire-agent-omp/AGENT.md:35:`omp` 17.1.1 can supersede a `before_agent_start` notification before the agent loop begins, so the adapter waits for `agent_start` before opening the Entire turn. Intermediate settles carry `willContinue: true`; they and repeated start events from automatic continuations stay within the existing turn. The final settle is forwarded synchronously so print-mode shutdown cannot discard the Entire TurnEnd event. Session switches and branches use the same reset path as initial loading, with any previous TurnEnd completed before the new SessionStart.

agents/entire-agent-kilo/README.md:3:Standalone external agent binary that teaches the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) how to work with [Kilo Code](https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode).
agents/entire-agent-kilo/README.md:7:- Installs a project plugin at `.kilo/plugins/entire.ts` that subscribes to Kilo's `event` bus.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/README.md:8:- Forwards five lifecycle hooks to the Entire CLI: `session-start`, `turn-start`, `turn-end`, `compaction`, `session-end`.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/README.md:9:- Fetches the authoritative session JSON via the local Kilo SDK client (`@kilocode/sdk`) on turn-end and writes it to `session_ref` so Entire can checkpoint without polling.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/README.md:10:- Maps Kilo's MessageV2 transcript into Entire's `AgentSessionJSON` envelope for compact transcripts, modified-file extraction, and token counting.

These same-user path checks are not a race-resistant filesystem boundary. Directory and file modes are restricted to `0700` and `0600`. agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:5:Kilo Code is a fork of OpenCode with a `@kilocode/plugin` API that exposes session lifecycle events on its internal event bus. Plugins are TypeScript/JavaScript modules loaded at startup from `.kilo/plugins/` and run on Bun. The integration installs a project plugin that subscribes to the bus and forwards five lifecycle hooks (`session-start`, `turn-start`, `turn-end`, `compaction`, `session-end`) to the Entire CLI. The plugin uses Kilo's native event bus directly — `session.idle` is deprecated upstream and `session.status` with `status.type === "idle"` is the reliable turn-end signal in both interactive and `kilo run` modes.

agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:104:- **Resume restore is EXPERIMENTAL / incomplete.** Kilo keeps sessions in a global store (`~/.local/share/kilo/kilo.db`) keyed by session id, not in `.entire/`. `entire resume` restores the transcript to `.entire/tmp/kilo/<id>.json` and prints `kilo run --session <id>`, but Kilo only reads its own store — so resume works **only while Kilo still has the session locally**. Restoring a session Entire has but Kilo does not (after `kilo session delete`, a fresh clone, or another machine) is **not yet supported**: it would require importing the session back into Kilo via `kilo import <file>` (Kilo exposes `kilo export [id]` / `kilo import <file>` for this). That needs the durable artifact to be Kilo's native export blob rather than the analysis-oriented JSONL stored today, and is tracked as future work. Everything else (checkpointing, attribution, summaries, transcript analysis) is unaffected. The agent is `is_preview: true` accordingly.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:105:- Kilo plugins do not load when `KILO_PURE=1` is set. The plugin must not assume that env is unset; if it is set, hooks never fire and `are-hooks-installed` still returns true (file exists).
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:106:- The transcript is materialized by `prepare-transcript` (Go side, via `kilo session show --format json` — see `command_runner.go`), which Entire calls before reading, mirroring the OpenCode parent. The plugin's `turn-end` fires **synchronously** and carries only `session_id` + `model`: `kilo run` exits on the same idle event, so an awaited in-plugin fetch could be cancelled before the hook runs. Turn-end payloads that do carry messages are still honored, but an empty message set never overwrites an existing transcript.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:107:- `session.idle` is deprecated upstream and not reliably emitted in `kilo run` mode. The plugin subscribes to `session.status` and filters on `status.type === "idle"` for turn-end.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:108:- Sub-sessions (Kilo subagent threads) are filtered out at `session.created` time by checking `info.parentID`. Subagent activity inside the parent session is still captured because the parent session JSON includes all parts.

agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:43:- Session cache: `.entire/tmp/kiro-active-session` is used exclusively for the Kiro-CLI (non-IDE) flow. IDE chats aren't cached as a "current session" because re-deriving from `<sessionId>.json` mtime each turn is what lets tab-switching scenarios resolve correctly
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:44:- Active turn cache: `.entire/tmp/kiro-active-turn` holds the IDE session ID for the in-flight turn — written at `user-prompt-submit`, read by `post-tool-use` and `stop`, cleared at end of `stop`. This binds an entire turn (prompt → tool uses → stop) to the chat that fired prompt-submit, so a tab switch mid-turn cannot cause stop to finalize against a different chat
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:45:- Per-chat trim offset: every IDE chat and every CLI `conversation_id` gets its own offset file (`.entire/tmp/kiro-transcript-offset-<key>.json`) so capturing one chat never trims another chat's history
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:46:- Per-chat tool-call capture: `post-tool-use` appends to a per-chat file (`.entire/tmp/kiro-tool-calls-<sanitized-id>.jsonl`) keyed by the active-turn cache; transcript capture reads only the current chat's file. The legacy global file is reserved for CLI-only flows where there is no IDE chat ID
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:49:- `kiro-active-turn` is a single repo-global file. Each prompt-submit overwrites it; each stop owner-checks before clearing. This is correct for the common cases — single chat, tab-switch mid-turn, sequential turns across tabs, and concurrent CLI+IDE activity (each side's payload lets the other flow stay isolated). It is best-effort under truly overlapping IDE turns (`A prompt → B prompt → A stop`): A's stop has no payload signal that distinguishes it from B's, so the resolver returns whichever IDE chat is currently in cache. The owner-check at clear time prevents A's stop from deleting B's binding, but A's session_id will still resolve to whatever the cache currently holds. Fixing this fully requires a per-turn signal in the hook payload from Kiro, which it does not provide today
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:50:- For the same reason, post-tool-use hooks during a truly overlapping IDE turn fall back to mtime-based active-chat detection when the cache holds the wrong chat. CLI flows are unaffected because they short-circuit on payload `conversation_id`

agents/entire-agent-amp/AGENT.md:5:Amp has a TypeScript plugin system with lifecycle events for `agent.start` and `agent.end`. Project plugins require launching Amp with `PLUGINS=all` in classic Amp clients. Amp threads are server-side, so the integration uses plugin hooks to discover the active thread ID and then retrieves the authoritative transcript with `amp threads export <thread-id>` directly from the `session.start` and `agent.end` hooks.

agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:5:Kilo Code is a fork of OpenCode with a `@kilocode/plugin` API that exposes session lifecycle events on its internal event bus. Plugins are TypeScript/JavaScript modules loaded at startup from `.kilo/plugins/` and run on Bun. The integration installs a project plugin that subscribes to the bus and forwards five lifecycle hooks (`session-start`, `turn-start`, `turn-end`, `compaction`, `session-end`) to the Entire CLI. The plugin uses Kilo's native event bus directly — `session.idle` is deprecated upstream and `session.status` with `status.type === "idle"` is the reliable turn-end signal in both interactive and `kilo run` modes.

agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:104:- **Resume restore is EXPERIMENTAL / incomplete.** Kilo keeps sessions in a global store (`~/.local/share/kilo/kilo.db`) keyed by session id, not in `.entire/`. `entire resume` restores the transcript to `.entire/tmp/kilo/<id>.json` and prints `kilo run --session <id>`, but Kilo only reads its own store — so resume works **only while Kilo still has the session locally**. Restoring a session Entire has but Kilo does not (after `kilo session delete`, a fresh clone, or another machine) is **not yet supported**: it would require importing the session back into Kilo via `kilo import <file>` (Kilo exposes `kilo export [id]` / `kilo import <file>` for this). That needs the durable artifact to be Kilo's native export blob rather than the analysis-oriented JSONL stored today, and is tracked as future work. Everything else (checkpointing, attribution, summaries, transcript analysis) is unaffected. The agent is `is_preview: true` accordingly.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:105:- Kilo plugins do not load when `KILO_PURE=1` is set. The plugin must not assume that env is unset; if it is set, hooks never fire and `are-hooks-installed` still returns true (file exists).
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:106:- The transcript is materialized by `prepare-transcript` (Go side, via `kilo session show --format json` — see `command_runner.go`), which Entire calls before reading, mirroring the OpenCode parent. The plugin's `turn-end` fires **synchronously** and carries only `session_id` + `model`: `kilo run` exits on the same idle event, so an awaited in-plugin fetch could be cancelled before the hook runs. Turn-end payloads that do carry messages are still honored, but an empty message set never overwrites an existing transcript.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:107:- `session.idle` is deprecated upstream and not reliably emitted in `kilo run` mode. The plugin subscribes to `session.status` and filters on `status.type === "idle"` for turn-end.
agents/entire-agent-kilo/AGENT.md:108:- Sub-sessions (Kilo subagent threads) are filtered out at `session.created` time by checking `info.parentID`. Subagent activity inside the parent session is still captured because the parent session JSON includes all parts.

agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:43:- Session cache: `.entire/tmp/kiro-active-session` is used exclusively for the Kiro-CLI (non-IDE) flow. IDE chats aren't cached as a "current session" because re-deriving from `<sessionId>.json` mtime each turn is what lets tab-switching scenarios resolve correctly
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:44:- Active turn cache: `.entire/tmp/kiro-active-turn` holds the IDE session ID for the in-flight turn — written at `user-prompt-submit`, read by `post-tool-use` and `stop`, cleared at end of `stop`. This binds an entire turn (prompt → tool uses → stop) to the chat that fired prompt-submit, so a tab switch mid-turn cannot cause stop to finalize against a different chat
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:45:- Per-chat trim offset: every IDE chat and every CLI `conversation_id` gets its own offset file (`.entire/tmp/kiro-transcript-offset-<key>.json`) so capturing one chat never trims another chat's history
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:46:- Per-chat tool-call capture: `post-tool-use` appends to a per-chat file (`.entire/tmp/kiro-tool-calls-<sanitized-id>.jsonl`) keyed by the active-turn cache; transcript capture reads only the current chat's file. The legacy global file is reserved for CLI-only flows where there is no IDE chat ID
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:49:- `kiro-active-turn` is a single repo-global file. Each prompt-submit overwrites it; each stop owner-checks before clearing. This is correct for the common cases — single chat, tab-switch mid-turn, sequential turns across tabs, and concurrent CLI+IDE activity (each side's payload lets the other flow stay isolated). It is best-effort under truly overlapping IDE turns (`A prompt → B prompt → A stop`): A's stop has no payload signal that distinguishes it from B's, so the resolver returns whichever IDE chat is currently in cache. The owner-check at clear time prevents A's stop from deleting B's binding, but A's session_id will still resolve to whatever the cache currently holds. Fixing this fully requires a per-turn signal in the hook payload from Kiro, which it does not provide today
agents/entire-agent-kiro/AGENT.md:50:- For the same reason, post-tool-use hooks during a truly overlapping IDE turn fall back to mtime-based active-chat detection when the cache holds the wrong chat. CLI flows are unaffected because they short-circuit on payload `conversation_id`

agents/entire-agent-amp/AGENT.md:5:Amp has a TypeScript plugin system with lifecycle events for `agent.start` and `agent.end`. Project plugins require launching Amp with `PLUGINS=all` in classic Amp clients. Amp threads are server-side, so the integration uses plugin hooks to discover the active thread ID and then retrieves the authoritative transcript with `amp threads export <thread-id>` directly from the `session.start` and `agent.end` hooks.

The command-line interface for Entire

Getting Started:
  To get started with Entire CLI, run 'entire enable' to enable
  session tracking in your repository, then 'entire agent add <name>'
  to install hooks for a specific agent. For more information, visit:
  https://docs.entire.io/overview


Environment Variables:
  ACCESSIBLE    Set to any value (e.g., ACCESSIBLE=1) to enable accessibility
                mode. This uses simpler text prompts instead of interactive
                TUI elements, which works better with screen readers.

Usage:
  entire [flags]
  entire [command]

Entire Setup:
  agent                      Manage agent integrations (add, remove, list)
  clean                      Clean up Entire session data
  configure                  Update Entire settings in the current repository
  disable                    Disable Entire in current repository
  doctor                     Diagnose and fix session issues
  enable                     Enable Entire in current repository
  plugin                     Manage Entire plugins (install, list, upgrade, search, remove)
  status                     Show Entire status

Sessions & Checkpoints:
  activity                   Show your activity overview
  checkpoint                 Inspect and search checkpoints
  dispatch                   Generate a dispatch summarizing recent agent work
  recap                      Summarize recent checkpoint activity
  search                     Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
  session                    Manage agent sessions tracked by Entire

Account:
  auth                       Manage authentication
  login                      Log in to Entire
  logout                     Log out of Entire

Control Plane:
  api                        Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
  grant                      Manage Entire access grants and org membership
  org                        Manage Entire organizations
  project                    Manage Entire projects
  repo                       Manage Entire repositories

Additional Commands:
  agent-help                 Machine-readable usage for coding agents (always matches the installed CLI)
  help                       Help about any command
  labs                       Explore experimental Entire workflows
  version                    Show build information

Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
  -h, --help           help for entire
  -v, --version        version for entire

Use "entire [command] --help" for more information about a command.

README.md:187:### Checkpoints
README.md:189:A **checkpoint** is a snapshot within a session—a "save point" in your work.
README.md:191:Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit, and the commit carries an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer linking the two.
README.md:193:**Checkpoint IDs** are 26-character ULIDs (e.g. `REDACTED`), which sort by creation time. Checkpoints written by older versions of Entire carry a legacy 12-character hex ID (e.g. `a3b2c4d5e6f7`); both formats stay readable in the same repo, and you can pass either to any command that takes a checkpoint ID.
README.md:195:### Checkpoint Storage
README.md:197:Checkpoints live in your repository's own git object store, never in your branch's history. Each checkpoint is its own git ref:
README.md:200:refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>
README.md:203:The ref points at a commit whose tree *is* that checkpoint — `metadata.json`, the per-session transcript files, and any subagent task records. `<shard>` is the last two characters of the ID, which keeps the refs evenly distributed.
README.md:205:Because checkpoints are independent refs, they are written, pushed, and fetched independently. There is no shared branch tip for concurrent sessions to contend on, and a reader can fetch exactly the one checkpoint it needs instead of a whole history. A checkpoint written on another machine is fetched on demand the first time you read it.

Operations on checkpoints — the persistent records of agent work tied to commits.

Commands:
  list     List checkpoints on the current branch
  explain  Explain a checkpoint, commit, or session
  tokens   Show token usage and optimization recommendations
  search   Search checkpoints (semantic + keyword)

Examples:
  entire checkpoint list
  entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>
  entire checkpoint tokens <id>
  entire checkpoint search "fix login"

Usage:
  entire checkpoint [command]

Aliases:
  checkpoint, cp, checkpoints

Available Commands:
  explain     Explain a session, commit, or checkpoint
  list        List checkpoints on the current branch
  search      Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
  tokens      Show token usage and optimization recommendations for a checkpoint

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for checkpoint

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Use "entire checkpoint [command] --help" for more information about a command.
Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire checkpoint explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Checkpoints in another repo:
  entire checkpoint explain <id> --repo owner/name
                 Explain a checkpoint owned by another repository — the
                 drill-down for a cross-repo 'entire search' hit. Reads it from
                 that repo's Entire API; nothing is written to this repo.
                 Needs a full checkpoint ID (positional or --checkpoint) and a
                 checkpoint that has been pushed.

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

Machine-readable export modes (additive surface for external consumers):
  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;
                   emits a single checkpoint envelope when a target is supplied.
                   Transcript bytes are NEVER embedded in the JSON envelope.
  --transcript     Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes (JSONL) to stdout
                   for the selected session. Same bytes as --raw-transcript
                   while checkpoints v1 is the checkpoint store.
  --session-index  Pick a session within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based).
                   Defaults to the latest session. Only meaningful with
                   --transcript or --raw-transcript.
  --limit          Cap the number of checkpoints returned by the list view.
                   Defaults to 100. When the cap is hit, a stderr note
                   says how many were skipped. Only meaningful with --json.

Summary generation:
  --generate    Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint
  --force       Regenerate even if a summary already exists (requires --generate)

Performance options:
  --search-all  Remove branch/depth limits when searching for commits (may be slow)

Checkpoint detail view shows:
  - Author of the checkpoint
  - Associated git commits that reference the checkpoint
  - Prompts and responses from the session

Note: --session filters the list view; the positional arg, --commit, and --checkpoint are mutually exclusive.

Usage:
  entire checkpoint explain [checkpoint-id | commit-sha] [flags]

Flags:
  -c, --checkpoint string             Explain a specific checkpoint (ID or prefix)
      --commit string                 Explain a specific commit (SHA or ref, "commit-ish")
      --force                         Regenerate summary even if one already exists (requires --generate)
      --full                          Show full parsed transcript (all prompts/responses)
      --generate                      Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint
  -h, --help                          help for explain
      --insecure-http-auth            Allow plain-HTTP auth for --repo (local dev only)
      --json                          Output metadata as JSON (no transcript bytes)
      --limit int                     Cap the list view at N checkpoints (default: 100). Only meaningful with --json.
      --no-pager                      Disable pager output
      --raw-transcript                Show raw transcript file (JSONL format)
      --repo string                   Explain a checkpoint owned by another repo (owner/name or gh/owner/name), read from that repo's Entire API
      --search-all                    Search all commits (no branch/depth limit, may be slow)
      --session string                Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)
      --session-index int             Session index within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based, defaults to latest) (default -1)
  -s, --short                         Show summary only (omit prompts and files)
      --summary-timeout-seconds int   Hard deadline in seconds for --generate summary generation; overrides summary_timeout_seconds setting. 0 = use setting; if setting is also unset or 0, no automatic deadline applies.
      --transcript                    Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes to stdout

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using hybrid search (semantic + keyword),
powered by the Entire search service.

Requires authentication via 'entire login' (GitHub device flow).

By default, results are scoped to the current repository. Use --all-repos to
search across all accessible repos.

Run without arguments to open an interactive search. Results are
displayed in an interactive table. Use --json for machine-readable output,
and add --compact for a trimmed per-result shape suited to agents (implies
--json): id, type, repo, branch, author, date, files touched, score, match
snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (repo hits add
description and checkpoint count). Fetch full detail
for a single result with 'entire checkpoint explain <id>', or add --full to
that command to pull the checkpoint's entire session transcript. For a
checkpoint hit from another GitHub repo, add --repo <owner/name> to
'entire checkpoint explain' (requires the full checkpoint ID; unrelated to
this command's --repo filter below).

CLI queries also support inline filters like author:<name>, date:<week|month>,
branch:<name>, repo:<owner/name>, and repo:* to search all accessible repos.

Usage:
  entire search [query] [flags]

Examples:
  entire search "retry backoff" --json
  entire search "retry backoff" --json --compact
  entire search "auth timeout author:alice date:week"
  entire search --code "parseToken"

Flags:
      --all-repos        Search all accessible repos instead of just the current one
      --author string    Filter by author name
      --branch string    Filter by branch name
      --case-sensitive   Case-sensitive code search (only with --code)
      --code             Search code content across repositories
      --compact          Trimmed JSON output for agents: id, repo, files touched, score, match snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (implies --json)
      --date string      Filter by time period (week or month)
  -h, --help             help for search
      --json             Output as JSON
      --limit int        Maximum number of results (per page for checkpoint search, total for --code) (default 10)
      --page int         Page number (1-based) (default 1)
      --repo strings     Filter by repository (gh/owner/repo, et/proj/repo, owner/repo, ULID, or *); repeatable and comma-separated for multiple repos

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

These endpoints are internal and can change shape without notice; where a
purpose-built command exists, its output is the stable interface.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

Usage:
  entire api <path> [flags]

Examples:
  entire api /api/v1/clusters
  entire api --to cell /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --jurisdiction eu /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}"
  entire api -X POST /api/v1/projects -f name=demo

Flags:
  -F, --field stringArray       add a typed parameter in key=value format; true/false/null/numbers are converted (repeatable)
  -H, --header stringArray      add a request header in key:value format (repeatable)
  -h, --help                    help for api
  -i, --include                 print the response status line and headers too
      --input string            file with the request body ("-" for stdin)
  -j, --jurisdiction string     target a specific jurisdiction's cell (e.g. us, eu) instead of your home cell; implies --to cell
  -X, --method string           HTTP method (default GET, or POST when a field/body is given)
  -f, --raw-field stringArray   add a string parameter in key=value format (repeatable)
      --to string               which backend to call: core or cell (default "core")

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
Prints agent-facing usage for the Entire CLI, generated live from the installed
command tree so it always matches this binary. With no arguments it prints a
high-level map of when to use entire and which subcommand; pass a command path
(e.g. "agent-help checkpoint") to see that command's exact, current flags.

Usage:
  entire agent-help [command...] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for agent-help
      --json   Emit structured JSON instead of text

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

1	# Entire CLI
     2	
     3	Entire hooks into your Git workflow to capture AI agent sessions as you work. Sessions are indexed alongside commits, creating a searchable record of how code was written in your repo.
     4	
     5	With Entire, you can:
     6	
     7	- **Understand why code changed** — see the full prompt/response transcript and files touched
     8	- **Recover instantly** — resume from a known-good checkpoint when an agent goes sideways
     9	- **Keep Git history clean** — agent context lives outside your branch's history
    10	- **Onboard faster** — show the path from prompt → change → commit
    11	- **Maintain traceability** — support audit and compliance requirements when needed
    12	
    13	## Why Entire
    14	
    15	- **Understand why code changed, not just what** — Transcripts, prompts, files touched, token usage, tool calls, and more are captured alongside every commit.
    16	- **Resume from any checkpoint** — Go back to any previous agent session and pick up exactly where you or a coworker left off.
    17	- **Full context preserved and searchable** — A versioned record of every AI interaction tied to your git history, with nothing lost.
    18	- **Zero context switching** — Git-native, two-step setup, works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, and more.
    19	
    20	## Table of Contents
    21	
    22	- [Why Entire](#why-entire)
    23	- [Requirements](#requirements)
    24	- [Quick Start](#quick-start)
    25	- [Release Channels](#release-channels)
    26	- [Typical Workflow](#typical-workflow)

    28	  - [Sessions](#sessions)
    29	  - [Checkpoints](#checkpoints)
    30	  - [Checkpoint Storage](#checkpoint-storage)
    31	  - [How It Works](#how-it-works)
    32	  - [Strategy](#strategy)
    33	- [Headless & CI Authentication](#headless--ci-authentication)
    34	- [Commands Reference](#commands-reference)
    35	- [Plugins](#plugins)
    36	- [Configuration](#configuration)
    37	- [Security & Privacy](#security--privacy)
    38	- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
    39	- [Development](#development)
    40	- [Getting Help](#getting-help)
    41	- [License](#license)
    42	
    43	## Requirements
    44	
    45	- Git
    46	- macOS, Linux or Windows
    47	- [Supported agent](#agent-hook-configuration) installed and authenticated
    48	- Go 1.26+ only if you install with `go install` (the packaged installs bundle their own runtime)
    49	
    50	## Quick Start
    51	
    52	### macOS and Linux
    53	
    54	Install with Homebrew:
    55	
    56	```bash
    57	brew tap entireio/tap
    58	brew trust entireio/tap
    59	brew install --cask entire            # stable
    60	# brew install --cask entire@nightly  # or nightly
    61	```
    62	
    63	Or with the install script:
    64	
    65	```bash
    66	curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash                          # stable
    67	# curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly  # or nightly
    68	```
    69	
    70	### Windows
    71	
    72	Install with Scoop:
    73	
    74	```powershell
    75	scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
    76	scoop install entire/entire
    77	```
    78	
    79	#### Migrating an old `cli` Scoop install (package rename)
    80	
    81	The Scoop package was renamed from `cli` to `entire`. If your install is still registered as the old `cli` package, run the migration below. It installs the new package before removing the old one, so the old install is only removed once the new one is in place (`scoop reset` re-links the shared `entire.exe` and `git-remote-entire.exe` shims). Run it where `entire` is **not** running — a live `entire.exe` locks its own shim, so Scoop can't relink or uninstall it mid-run:
    82	
    83	```powershell
    84	cmd.exe /D /C "scoop install entire/entire && scoop uninstall entire/cli && scoop reset entire"
    85	```
    86	
    87	If the first step fails with "couldn't find manifest", your bucket clone predates the renamed package — run `scoop update` to refresh it, then retry the command above. Nothing is removed until the install succeeds, so a failed attempt leaves your existing install working.
    88	
    89	### Go (development/manual setup)
    90	
    91	```bash
    92	go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest
    93	
    94	# The git remote helper that resolves entire:// URLs, needed for `entire repo clone`
    95	# and `git clone entire://…`. The packaged installs above bundle it.
    96	go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/git-remote-entire@latest
    97	
    98	# Add Go binaries to PATH (add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc if not already configured)
    99	export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"
   100	```
   101	
   102	Install both, or just `entire` if you never clone over `entire://`. Git finds the helper by name on `$PATH`, which is what `go install` produces, so nothing else needs configuring.
   103	
   104	One difference from a stable release: a `go install` build leaves [experimental commands](#experimental-commands) visible in `entire help`, the same as a nightly or a local build.
   105	
   106	### Enable in your project
   107	
   108	```bash
   109	cd your-project && entire enable
   110	
   111	# Check status
   112	entire status
   113	```
   114	
   115	After the initial setup, use `entire agent` to add or remove agents, `entire configure` to update non-agent settings, and `entire enable` / `entire disable` to toggle Entire on or off.
   116	
   117	## Release Channels
   118	
   119	Entire currently ships two release channels:
   120	
   121	- `stable`: recommended for most users. Stable releases change less often and are the default for Homebrew, Scoop, and `install.sh`.
   122	- `nightly`: prerelease builds for users who want the latest changes earlier. Nightlies are published more frequently and may include newer, less-proven changes than stable.
   123	
   124	How to use each channel:
   125	
   126	- Homebrew (one-time setup): `brew tap entireio/tap && brew trust entireio/tap`
   127	- Homebrew stable: `brew install --cask entire`
   128	- Homebrew nightly: `brew install --cask entire@nightly`
   129	- `install.sh` stable: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`
   130	- `install.sh` nightly: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly`
   131	- Scoop: currently supports `stable` only via `scoop install entire/entire`
   132	
   133	## Typical Workflow
   134	
   135	### 1. Enable Entire in Your Repository
   136	
   137	```
   138	entire enable
   139	```
   140	
   141	On a repo that has not been enabled yet, `entire enable` runs the initial enable flow: it creates Entire settings, installs git hooks, and prompts you to choose which agent hooks to install. To enable a specific agent non-interactively, use `entire enable --agent <name>` (for example, `entire enable --agent cursor`).
   142	
   143	After setup:
   144	
   145	- Use `entire enable` to turn Entire back on if the repo is currently disabled.
   146	- Use `entire agent` to add or remove agents.
   147	- Use `entire configure` to update non-agent settings (telemetry, hooks, checkpoint remote, summary provider).
   148	
   149	The hooks capture session data as you work. Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit. Your code commits stay clean, Entire never creates commits on your active branch. Session metadata is stored outside your branch's history, in the checkpoint storage described under [Checkpoint Storage](#checkpoint-storage).
   150	
   151	### 2. Work with Your AI Agent
   152	
   153	Just use one of your AI agents as before. Entire runs in the background, tracking your session:
   154	
   155	```
   156	entire status  # Check current session status anytime
   157	```
   158	
   159	### 3. Resume a Previous Session
   160	
   161	To restore the latest checkpointed session metadata for a branch:
   162	
   163	```
   164	entire session resume <branch>
   165	```
   166	
   167	Entire checks out the branch, restores the latest checkpointed session metadata (one or more sessions), and prints command(s) to continue.
   168	
   169	### 4. Disable Entire (Optional)
   170	
   171	```
   172	entire disable
   173	```
   174	
   175	Removes the git hooks. Your code and commit history remain untouched.
   176	
   177	## Key Concepts
   178	
   179	### Sessions
   180	
   181	A **session** represents a complete interaction with your AI agent, from start to finish. Each session captures all prompts, responses, files modified, and timestamps.
   182	
   183	The session ID is the unique identifier the agent itself provides — Entire never mints its own — so an ID you see in `entire session list` is the same one the agent uses. The format is the agent's to choose: most supply a UUID (e.g. `019efea2-b46a-7cbc-be01-4c13460f5019`), while OpenCode uses `ses_`-prefixed IDs.
   184	
   185	Sessions are stored separately from your code commits, in the repo's checkpoint storage.
   186	
   187	### Checkpoints
   188	
   189	A **checkpoint** is a snapshot within a session—a "save point" in your work.
   190	
   191	Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit, and the commit carries an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer linking the two.
   192	
   193	**Checkpoint IDs** are 26-character ULIDs (e.g. `REDACTED`), which sort by creation time. Checkpoints written by older versions of Entire carry a legacy 12-character hex ID (e.g. `a3b2c4d5e6f7`); both formats stay readable in the same repo, and you can pass either to any command that takes a checkpoint ID.
   194	
   195	### Checkpoint Storage
   196	
   197	Checkpoints live in your repository's own git object store, never in your branch's history. Each checkpoint is its own git ref:
   198	
   199	```
   200	refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>
   201	```
   202	
   203	The ref points at a commit whose tree *is* that checkpoint — `metadata.json`, the per-session transcript files, and any subagent task records. `<shard>` is the last two characters of the ID, which keeps the refs evenly distributed.
   204	
   205	Because checkpoints are independent refs, they are written, pushed, and fetched independently. There is no shared branch tip for concurrent sessions to contend on, and a reader can fetch exactly the one checkpoint it needs instead of a whole history. A checkpoint written on another machine is fetched on demand the first time you read it.
   206	
   207	`entire enable` sets this up; there is nothing to configure. It is recorded in `.entire/settings.json` as:
   208	
   209	```json
   210	{
   211	  "checkpoints": {
   212	    "primary": { "type": "git-refs" }
   213	  }
   214	}
   215	```
   216	
   217	Inspect what a repo has locally with plain git, or through Entire:
   218	
   219	```bash
   220	git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints    # the raw refs
   221	entire checkpoint list                      # checkpoints on this branch
   222	entire checkpoint explain <id>              # one checkpoint in full
   223	```
   224	
   225	### How It Works
   226	
   227	```
   228	Your Branch                      Checkpoint storage
   229	     │                                  │
   230	     ▼                                  │

   437	## Plugins
   438	
   439	Plugins extend the CLI with new verbs: any executable named `entire-<name>` on `$PATH` runs as `entire <name>`, kubectl-style — stdio passes through, exit codes propagate, no SDK or protocol required.
   440	
   441	```sh
   442	entire plugin search                                    # search the plugin index
   443	entire plugin browse                                    # browse the index interactively and install
   444	entire plugin install run                               # install by name (index lookup)
   445	entire plugin install https://github.com/you/entire-x   # install from any git host
   446	entire plugin install ./dist/entire-x                   # link a local build
   447	entire plugin list                                      # list what's installed
   448	entire run                                              # run an installed plugin
   449	entire plugin upgrade --all                             # update remote-installed plugins
   450	entire plugin doctor                                    # check for broken installs and missing dependencies
   451	entire plugin remove run
   452	```
   453	
   454	Remote installs are forge-agnostic: the newest stable semver tag is resolved over the git protocol (prereleases need an explicit `--pin`), and the platform's release asset is downloaded over HTTPS and verified against the release's `checksums.txt`. A release that publishes no checksums is refused unless you pass `--allow-unverified` — installing means making those bytes executable. `entire plugin doctor` re-checks installed binaries against the digests recorded at install time. Plugins can declare dependencies on other plugins in an `entire-plugin.yml`; missing ones are installed after a single confirmation.
   455	
   456	Discovery uses a git-synced catalog, [entireio/plugin-index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index) by default. Organizations can point the CLI at an internal catalog with the `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL` environment variable or `--index`. It is deliberately not settable from a repository's committed settings: an index-listed plugin installs without a prompt, so a checked-out repo must not be able to choose the catalog.
   457	
   458	For the full contract — resolution rules, environment filtering, release-asset conventions, and how to author a plugin — see [External Commands](docs/architecture/external-commands.md).

   460	## Configuration
   461	
   462	Entire uses two configuration files in the `.entire/` directory:
   463	
   464	### settings.json (Project Settings)
   465	
   466	Shared across the team, typically committed to git. This is what `entire enable` writes for a new repo:
   467	
   468	```json
   469	{
   470	  "enabled": true,
   471	  "checkpoints": {
   472	    "primary": { "type": "git-refs" }
   473	  }
   474	}
   475	```
   476	
   477	### settings.local.json (Local Settings)
   478	
   479	Personal overrides, gitignored by default:
   480	
   481	```json
   482	{
   483	  "enabled": false,
   484	  "log_level": "debug"
   485	}
   486	```
   487	
   488	### Configuration Options
   489	
   490	| Option                                    | Values                                       | Description                                                                       |
   491	| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   492	| `enabled`                                 | `true`, `false`                              | Enable/disable Entire                                                             |
   493	| `log_level`                               | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`             | Logging verbosity                                                                 |
   494	| `checkpoints.primary.type`                | `git-refs`                                   | Checkpoint storage backend — written by `entire enable`, see [Checkpoint Storage](#checkpoint-storage) |
   495	| `telemetry`                               | `true`, `false`                              | Send anonymous usage statistics to Posthog                                        |
   496	| `absolute_git_hook_path`                  | `true`, `false`                              | Embed the full binary path in git hooks, for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles |
   497	| `commit_linking`                          | `always`, `prompt`                           | Link commits to sessions automatically, or ask each time (default `prompt`)        |
   498	| `sign_checkpoint_commits`                 | `true`, `false`                              | Sign checkpoint commits (default: on). See [checkpoint signing](docs/architecture/checkpoint-signing.md) |
   499	| `strategy_options.push_sessions`          | `true`, `false`                              | Auto-push checkpoint data on git push (default `true`)                            |
   500	| `strategy_options.checkpoint_remote`      | `{"provider": "github", "repo": "org/repo"}` | Push checkpoint data to a separate repo (see below)                               |
   501	| `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` | remote name, e.g. `"upstream"`               | Pin which single remote carries checkpoint data (see below)                       |
   502	| `strategy_options.filtered_fetches`       | `true`, `false`                              | Use `--filter=blob:none` on checkpoint fetches                                    |
   503	| `strategy_options.summarize.enabled`      | `true`, `false`                              | Auto-generate AI summaries at commit time                                         |
   504	| `summary_generation.provider`             | e.g. `claude-code`, `codex`, `gemini`        | Which agent generates summaries (defaults to Claude)                              |
   505	| `summary_generation.model`                | provider-specific model hint                 | Model hint for summary generation (requires `provider`)                            |
   506	| `summary_timeout_seconds`                 | seconds                                      | Hard deadline for `entire checkpoint explain --generate`. Unset or `0` means **no deadline** |
   507	| `redaction.*`                             | nested object                                | PII redaction, custom secret patterns, scanner engines, and the OpenAI Privacy Filter — documented in [docs/security-and-privacy.md](docs/security-and-privacy.md) |
   508	
   509	### Agent Hook Configuration
   510	
   511	Each agent stores its hook configuration in its own directory. When you run `entire enable`, hooks are installed in the appropriate location for each selected agent:
   512	
   513	| Agent            | Hook Location                 | Format            |
   514	| ---------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------- |
   515	| Claude Code      | `.claude/settings.json`       | JSON hooks config |
   516	| Codex            | `.codex/hooks.json`           | JSON hooks config |
   517	| Copilot CLI      | `.github/hooks/entire.json`   | JSON hooks config |
   518	| Cursor           | `.cursor/hooks.json`          | JSON hooks config |
   519	| Factory AI Droid | `.factory/settings.json`      | JSON hooks config |
   520	| Gemini CLI       | `.gemini/settings.json`       | JSON hooks config |
   521	| OpenCode         | `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` | TypeScript plugin |
   522	| Pi               | `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` | TypeScript extension |
   523	
   524	You can enable multiple agents at the same time — each agent's hooks are independent. Entire detects which agents are active by checking for installed hooks, not by a setting in `settings.json`.
   525	
   526	### Checkpoint Remote
   527	
   528	By default, checkpoint data rides along with your own pushes — but only to **one** remote, the elected checkpoint sync remote. Entire picks it in this order:
   529	
   530	1. `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote`, if set. This is fail-closed: if it names a remote that isn't configured, checkpoints don't sync.
   531	2. A remote captured from your own habits: the first push whose target matches the branch's declared push destination elects that remote, announces it on stderr, and carries the checkpoints. The first capture sticks.
   532	3. `origin`
   533	4. The sole remote, if the repo has exactly one
   534	5. The first remote in `.git/config` order
   535	
   536	A push to any *other* remote carries no checkpoint data. `entire status` shows the current destination, where it came from, and how many checkpoints are unpushed. This matters if you push code to several remotes: checkpoints go to exactly one of them.
   537	
   538	If instead you want checkpoint data in a separate repo (e.g., a private repo for a public project), configure `checkpoint_remote` with a structured provider and repo. A dedicated `checkpoint_remote` is addressed directly and is exempt from the single-remote election above:
   539	
   540	```json
   541	{
   542	  "strategy_options": {
   543	    "checkpoint_remote": {
   544	      "provider": "github",
   545	      "repo": "myorg/checkpoints-private"
   546	    }
   547	  }
   548	}
   549	```
   550	
   551	Or via the CLI:
   552	
   553	```bash
   554	entire enable --checkpoint-remote github:myorg/checkpoints-private
   555	```
   556	
   557	Entire derives the git URL automatically using the same protocol (SSH or HTTPS) as your push remote. It will:
   558	
   559	- Fetch existing checkpoint data locally if the remote has it and you don't (one-time)
   560	- Push checkpoint data to the checkpoint repo instead of your default push remote
   561	- Ignore the setting if it looks inherited rather than yours, and fall back to `origin` (or, failing that, the remote you are pushing to). `checkpoint_remote` is normally committed in `.entire/settings.json`, so cloning or forking a project inherits it — without this, a contributor's session data would be pushed into the upstream project's checkpoint repo. A setting is treated as yours when it lives in the gitignored `.entire/settings.local.json`, or when your `origin` **and every push URL** of the remote you are pushing to are owned by the same account or org as the checkpoint repo. Requiring the push destination too covers contributors who cloned the upstream repo and added their own fork, where `origin` belongs to the upstream project rather than to them; requiring every push URL covers mirror-style remotes that fan out to several repositories
   562	- If your checkpoint repo is owned by a different account or org than `origin`, configure it in `.entire/settings.local.json` so it is always honored
   563	- If the remote is unreachable, warn and continue without blocking your main push
   564	
   565	#### `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`
   566	
   567	`ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` allows you to provide a dedicated token for checkpoint repository operations, without modifying the credentials used for your primary repository.
   568	
   569	When this environment variable is set, Entire behaves as follows:
   570	
   571	- Injects the token into HTTPS Git operations used for checkpoint fetch and push
   572	- If `checkpoint_remote` is configured:
   573	  - Prefers an HTTPS URL for the checkpoint remote when a token is present, even if the repository’s `origin` uses SSH
   574	- If `checkpoint_remote` is not configured:
   575	  - Falls back to using the default `origin` remote
   576	- If `checkpoint_remote` configuration cannot be loaded:
   577	  - Falls back to `origin`
   578	  - If `origin` is a valid SSH or HTTPS Git remote, Entire converts it to an HTTPS URL to enable token-based authentication
   579	
   580	### Auto-Summarization
   581	
   582	When enabled, Entire automatically generates AI summaries for checkpoints at commit time. Summaries capture intent, outcome, learnings, friction points, and open items from the session.
   583	
   584	```json
   585	{
   586	  "strategy_options": {
   587	    "summarize": {
   588	      "enabled": true
   589	    }
   590	  }
   591	}
   592	```
   593	
   594	Summaries are also generated on demand, with or without this setting, by `entire checkpoint explain --generate`.
   595	
   596	**Which agent writes them.** By default Claude Code (`claude` on your `PATH`, model `sonnet`). Set a different one with `summary_generation.provider` — `claude-code`, `codex`, `copilot-cli`, `cursor`, `gemini`, or `pi`, plus an optional `summary_generation.model` hint:
   597	
   598	```bash
   599	entire configure --summarize-provider codex
   600	```
   601	
   602	`opencode` and `factoryai-droid` cannot generate summaries. Whichever provider you pick must be installed and authenticated.
   603	
   604	**Requirements:**
   605	
   606	- The configured provider's CLI installed and authenticated
   607	- Summary generation is non-blocking: failures are logged but don't prevent commits
   608	
   609	### Settings Priority
   610	
   611	Local settings override project settings field-by-field. `entire status --detailed` shows the state of each settings file.
   612	
   613	Two exceptions to field-by-field merging:
   614	
   615	- The `checkpoints` block is **replaced wholesale** by the local one, not deep-merged — it selects a backend, so a half-merged block would be meaningless.
   616	- A `settings.local.json` that is **tracked in git** is ignored entirely, and Entire tells you to `git rm --cached` it. `.gitignore` doesn't apply to an already-tracked path, so a committed local file would otherwise override project settings for everyone who clones.
   617	
   618	### Agent-Specific Steps & Limitations
   619	
   620	- Codex hooks are enabled by default (codex-cli 0.124.0+), so enabling Entire for Codex only installs `.codex/hooks.json` — no `config.toml` is needed and Entire never creates one. If an older Entire version left a `.codex/config.toml` behind and your repo lives inside `~/.codex/agents`, delete that file to stop Codex's "malformed agent role definition" startup warning.
   621	- Entire supports Cursor IDE and Cursor Agent CLI tool. Commands (`doctor`, `status` etc.) work the same as all other agents.
   622	- Entire supports Copilot CLI, but not Copilot in VS Code, in other IDEs, or on github.com.
   623	- Entire supports Pi coding agent (Preview). Pi uses a TypeScript extension instead of a JSON hook config. Subagent capture is not currently available.
   624	
   625	## Security & Privacy
   626	
   627	**Your session transcripts are stored in your git repository**, in the [per-checkpoint refs](#checkpoint-storage) described above. If your repository is public, this data is visible to anyone.
   628	
   629	Entire automatically redacts detected secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) from transcripts and metadata before writing a checkpoint, but redaction is best-effort.
   630	
   631	The temporary shadow branches used during a session get the same redaction for transcripts and metadata, but their **code-file snapshots are raw blobs of your working tree**, so a secret hardcoded in your source appears unredacted there. Entire never pushes shadow branches — don't push them manually. See [docs/security-and-privacy.md](docs/security-and-privacy.md) for the full picture, including the configurable scanner layers, opt-in PII redaction, and the OpenAI Privacy Filter pass.

   437	## Plugins
   438	
   439	Plugins extend the CLI with new verbs: any executable named `entire-<name>` on `$PATH` runs as `entire <name>`, kubectl-style — stdio passes through, exit codes propagate, no SDK or protocol required.
   440	
   441	```sh
   442	entire plugin search                                    # search the plugin index
   443	entire plugin browse                                    # browse the index interactively and install
   444	entire plugin install run                               # install by name (index lookup)
   445	entire plugin install https://github.com/you/entire-x   # install from any git host
   446	entire plugin install ./dist/entire-x                   # link a local build
   447	entire plugin list                                      # list what's installed
   448	entire run                                              # run an installed plugin
   449	entire plugin upgrade --all                             # update remote-installed plugins
   450	entire plugin doctor                                    # check for broken installs and missing dependencies
   451	entire plugin remove run
   452	```
   453	
   454	Remote installs are forge-agnostic: the newest stable semver tag is resolved over the git protocol (prereleases need an explicit `--pin`), and the platform's release asset is downloaded over HTTPS and verified against the release's `checksums.txt`. A release that publishes no checksums is refused unless you pass `--allow-unverified` — installing means making those bytes executable. `entire plugin doctor` re-checks installed binaries against the digests recorded at install time. Plugins can declare dependencies on other plugins in an `entire-plugin.yml`; missing ones are installed after a single confirmation.
   455	
   456	Discovery uses a git-synced catalog, [entireio/plugin-index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index) by default. Organizations can point the CLI at an internal catalog with the `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL` environment variable or `--index`. It is deliberately not settable from a repository's committed settings: an index-listed plugin installs without a prompt, so a checked-out repo must not be able to choose the catalog.
   457	
   458	For the full contract — resolution rules, environment filtering, release-asset conventions, and how to author a plugin — see [External Commands](docs/architecture/external-commands.md).

A setting is treated as yours when it lives in the gitignored `.entire/settings.local.json`, or when your `origin` **and every push URL** of the remote you are pushing to are owned by the same account or org as the checkpoint repo. Requiring the push destination too covers contributors who cloned the upstream repo and added their own fork, where `origin` belongs to the upstream project rather than to them; requiring every push URL covers mirror-style remotes that fan out to several repositories
   562	- If your checkpoint repo is owned by a different account or org than `origin`, configure it in `.entire/settings.local.json` so it is always honored
   563	- If the remote is unreachable, warn and continue without blocking your main push

   565	#### `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`
   566	
   567	`ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` allows you to provide a dedicated token for checkpoint repository operations, without modifying the credentials used for your primary repository.
   568	
   569	When this environment variable is set, Entire behaves as follows:
   570	
   571	- Injects the token into HTTPS Git operations used for checkpoint fetch and push
   572	- If `checkpoint_remote` is configured:
   573	  - Prefers an HTTPS URL for the checkpoint remote when a token is present, even if the repository’s `origin` uses SSH
   574	- If `checkpoint_remote` is not configured:
   575	  - Falls back to using the default `origin` remote
   576	- If `checkpoint_remote` configuration cannot be loaded:
   577	  - Falls back to `origin`
   578	  - If `origin` is a valid SSH or HTTPS Git remote, Entire converts it to an HTTPS URL to enable token-based authentication

   580	### Auto-Summarization
   581	
   582	When enabled, Entire automatically generates AI summaries for checkpoints at commit time. Summaries capture intent, outcome, learnings, friction points, and open items from the session.
   583	
   584	```json
   585	{
   586	  "strategy_options": {
   587	    "summarize": {
   588	      "enabled": true
   589	    }
   590	  }
   591	}
   592	```
   593	
   594	Summaries are also generated on demand, with or without this setting, by `entire checkpoint explain --generate`.
   595	
   596	**Which agent writes them.** By default Claude Code (`claude` on your `PATH`, model `sonnet`). Set a different one with `summary_generation.provider` — `claude-code`, `codex`, `copilot-cli`, `cursor`, `gemini`, or `pi`, plus an optional `summary_generation.model` hint:
   597	
   598	```bash
   599	entire configure --summarize-provider codex
   600	```
   601	
   602	`opencode` and `factoryai-droid` cannot generate summaries. Whichever provider you pick must be installed and authenticated.
   603	
   604	**Requirements:**
   605	
   606	- The configured provider's CLI installed and authenticated
   607	- Summary generation is non-blocking: failures are logged but don't prevent commits

   609	### Settings Priority
   610	
   611	Local settings override project settings field-by-field. `entire status --detailed` shows the state of each settings file.
   612	
   613	Two exceptions to field-by-field merging:
   614	
   615	- The `checkpoints` block is **replaced wholesale** by the local one, not deep-merged — it selects a backend, so a half-merged block would be meaningless.
   616	- A `settings.local.json` that is **tracked in git** is ignored entirely, and Entire tells you to `git rm --cached` it. `.gitignore` doesn't apply to an already-tracked path, so a committed local file would otherwise override project settings for everyone who clones.

   625	## Security & Privacy
   626	
   627	**Your session transcripts are stored in your git repository**, in the [per-checkpoint refs](#checkpoint-storage) described above. If your repository is public, this data is visible to anyone.
   628	
   629	Entire automatically redacts detected secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) from transcripts and metadata before writing a checkpoint, but redaction is best-effort.
   630	
   631	The temporary shadow branches used during a session get the same redaction for transcripts and metadata, but their **code-file snapshots are raw blobs of your working tree**, so a secret hardcoded in your source appears unredacted there. Entire never pushes shadow branches — don't push them manually. See [docs/security-and-privacy.md](docs/security-and-privacy.md) for the full picture, including the configurable scanner layers, opt-in PII redaction, and the OpenAI Privacy Filter pass.
